headline: Brief 2–3 on the close, 1–4 on the first hour. The trades went 5–0 anyway — the edge is the open tape, not the brief's direction call.
learned: Gap direction was right 5 of 5 — the most reliable thing on the card.
The close call has no edge yet: 7–11 all-time, mean Brier 0.256 (worse than always saying 50%). Every call this week sat at 51–53%.
Gap size went stale twice (10-20, 10-23): the brief runs ~7:52 ET and futures kept moving. On 10-23 a 9:25 recheck would have fired R1, which was right.
Day type said NORMAL all week from VIX 17–20, but actual ranges were 0.60–1.05% — QUIET-like on 4 of 5 days.
Oil/Iran headlines had no open→close effect again (W6 now 14 days of evidence): Brent hit $116, SPY didn't care.
The AI-capex driver was under-weighted on 10-22 (earnings cluster kept selling all day) and over-weighted on 10-23 (day-2 bounce, now rule R2).
improve: Add a 6:20 AM PT gap recheck push: gap size, whether R1 fires, VIX.
Grade the first 15 minutes, not just the close — that is the window actually traded.
Call NO EDGE when the final probability is under 53% instead of a 51% lean.
Recalibrate day type with the last 10 days' realized range alongside VIX.
Prune the watching list from 16 to ~8 (drop W8 at 2 of 5, merge W13 into W15).
trading_notes: Best mechanics yet: cheaper premiums, out within 5–15 minutes of the open, one contract, no averaging.
All 3 losses this month came on days the trade followed the brief; the 4 trades against it went 4–0. Small sample, consistent message.
Average loss is about 2× the average win — a stop near −30% of premium fixes the ratio.
Behind the 5%/day path; the risk is sizing up to catch up.
rule_changes: R2 adopted (day-2 sector selloff: score 0, cap 52%)
W16 and W17 added to watching
